info.title: Backup Manager /api/v1
info.summary: The authoritative definition of the versioned /api/v1 boundary.
info.description: Issue #166 (B6.2). This document, not the Go handlers and not the TypeScript client, is the definition of /api/v1. Both sides are generated from it (scripts/api/generate.sh) and both are held to it by a drift check (scripts/api/check-contract-drift.sh plus the conformance tests named in docs/api/contract.md). Compatibility and deprecation rules are in docs/api/contract.md.

servers.description: Every path in this document is relative to the versioned base path. /health/live and /health/ready are deliberately NOT in this contract: they sit outside /api/v1, carry no authentication and exist for an orchestrator, not for a client of this API.

session.name: bm_session
session.description: The authenticated session. For the generic runtime profile this is apps/common/auth/local's own HTTP-only cookie; a runtime profile with a native gateway (native_auth) establishes the same session from provider identity headers accepted only from a trusted peer. Which mechanism established it is a profile concern; that a caller of a secured operation has one is not.

csrf.name: X-CSRF-Token
csrf.description: The double-submit CSRF token (apps/common/csrf). Required on every state-changing operation, and on the two read-only-in-effect operations that still open an outbound connection to a caller-supplied host.

bootstrapToken.name: X-Bootstrap-Token
bootstrapToken.description: The single-use enrollment secret printed to the runtime's own log. Only /auth/enroll accepts it.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Caller-supplied key that makes a retried submission a replay rather than a second operation. Reusing one key for two different operation bodies is IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT, never a silent second run.

ApiErrorCode.description: Every error code this API contract knows. `wire` codes are the machine-readable tokens a server may put on the wire; `ui` codes are the shared web UI's own presentation vocabulary, which no endpoint ever emits and which is listed here so there is exactly one registry rather than a second hand-maintained copy in ui/shared. `unknown` is the sentinel an unrecognised code off the network degrades to.

VersionResponse.description: GET /system/version. Nothing here names an implementation: no rclone, no SQLite, no filesystem path.

engine_version.description: The transfer engine's own version string, deliberately not named after the engine.

config_revision.description: The optimistic-concurrency token a client echoes back on POST /operations. Read here rather than scraped out of a 409's prose.

ready.description: True once the runtime has completed its startup sequence.

CapabilitiesResponse.description: GET /system/capabilities. The API expression of the PlatformCapabilities contract (apps/common/platform/capabilities). A capability says what a platform CAN do; it never says who MAY do it, and server-side authorization never consults it.

platform.description: The runtime profile's stable platform identifier.

local_path.description: The configured destination directory for this set, as the operator entered it.

free_bytes.description: Observability only. level is decided from available_bytes.

SubmitOperationRequest.description: POST /operations. The idempotency key is a header, not a body field: it is a property of the retry, not of the operation.

action.description: What to submit. An enumerated action name, never a command line.

config_revision.description: Optimistic concurrency: the revision the caller believes is current. A stale value is refused with CONFIG_REVISION_STALE and nothing runs.

Operation.description: One durable operation record. Timestamp fields are omitted, not zero-valued, until the event they name has happened.

RetentionVerdict.description: What the plan decided for one artifact, and why.

RetentionPlan.description: A server-computed retention plan. The client may only apply one by id; it never proposes what to delete.

inventory_revision.description: Optimistic concurrency, half one: the inventory this plan was computed against.

config_revision.description: Optimistic concurrency, half two: the configuration this plan was computed against. Either moving makes the plan stale and the apply is refused.

operation_id.description: Set on apply, absent on preview.

plan_id.description: The plan the operator approved. A plan the server no longer recognises, or one computed against a moved revision, is refused.

CreateBackupSetRequest.description: POST /backup-sets. ssh_key_id and known_hosts_line carry REFERENCES produced by /ssh-keys and /ssh/host-key-probe, never key material.

validator_id.description: A registered validator's id from GET /validators. Never a path, never a command.

run_immediately.description: Also submit a run_cycle. This branch, and only this branch, is subject to the destructive gate.

BackupSet.description: A persisted backup set as the API reports it.

CreateBackupSetResponse.description: POST /backup-sets. The created set, plus at most one of operation (the run_immediately branch started) or run_error (it did not). Always 201: the set itself exists either way.

allOf.description: The create-only additions on top of the backup set itself.

ListBackupSetsResponse.description: GET /backup-sets. An object with one array field, never a bare top-level array.

ImportSSHKeyRequest.description: POST /ssh-keys. Sent once; the caller discards its own copy immediately.

private_key_pem.description: Private key material. Write-only: it is never echoed back by any operation in this contract.

ImportSSHKeyResponse.description: The reference a later create-backup-set call carries instead of key material.

HostKeyProbeRequest.description: POST /ssh/host-key-probe. Opens a real outbound connection, trusts nothing.

HostKeyProbeResponse.description: What the server actually saw. Presenting it to an operator for approval is the caller's job.

TestConnectionRequest.description: POST /backup-sets/test-connection. A pre-save reachability and authentication check, before a backup set has an id.

TestConnectionResponse.description: The outcome of a pre-save connection test.

Validator.description: One registered application validator. An id and a sentence, and deliberately nothing else: the script it resolves to is server-side and a client never learns it.

ListValidatorsResponse.description: GET /validators. Read-only by design: a client-extensible catalog would be an arbitrary-command surface.

RetentionTier.description: One link in the retention chain, on the wire. The same shape is read and written, so a client round-trips exactly what it was served.

RetentionSettings.description: The retention policy actually in effect. tiers is always the RESOLVED chain.

protect_last_known_good.description: Turning this off widens what a later retention apply may delete. The apply itself stays behind the destructive gate.

RetentionSchema.description: The closed value sets and bounds a retention chain is validated against, served rather than transcribed into a frontend.

SettingsSchema.description: The schema half of the settings response.

SettingsResponse.description: GET and PATCH /settings both return this: the settings now in effect plus the rules they were validated against.

UpdateRetentionSettings.description: A PARTIAL retention update. An omitted field is left exactly as the running configuration has it; omitting tiers leaves the chain, and a legacy file's own spelling of it, untouched.

UpdateSettingsRequest.description: PATCH /settings. An enumerated request type, never a configuration passthrough.

CredentialsRequest.description: POST /auth/login and POST /auth/enroll. camelCase, unlike every schema above: apps/common/auth/local predates the snake_case convention the rest of /api/v1 uses. Recorded here as it is rather than silently normalised; see docs/api/contract.md for why fixing it is a separate issue.

RotatePasswordRequest.description: POST /auth/password. Requires an already-authenticated session AND the current password: holding a cookie is not enough.

ErrorBody.description: The nested error body every operation outside /auth returns. code is stable and machine-readable; message is human-readable and MAY change without notice.

ErrorResponse.description: The error envelope every operation outside /auth returns. The correlation id travels in the X-Correlation-Id response header.

ConfigRevisionStaleResponse.description: The CONFIG_REVISION_STALE 409 body. It carries the current revision as a structured field so a client retries against a value it can rely on rather than one parsed out of prose.

AuthErrorResponse.description: The FLAT error body the /auth operations return, with the correlation id in the body as well as the header. Deliberately recorded as a second shape rather than pretended away: apps/common/auth/local diverged from the envelope above before this contract existed.

get.summary: Version, build identity and the current configuration revision.
What this runtime profile's host platform can do for the product.
Compute, but do not apply, a retention plan. Read-only.

post.summary: Apply a plan the operator already approved, by id. The one operation in this contract that deletes local restore points.
Persist a new backup set, and optionally start its first run.
Reachability and authentication check for a set that does not exist yet. Carries CSRF because it opens an outbound connection to a caller-supplied host.

get.summary: Read one backup set. The id is a two-part source/name identity, so it spans path segments.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The two-part identity, e.g. "nas-a/photos". Registered in the router as a catch-all for exactly that reason.

post.summary: Import a private key and get back a reference to it.
Fetch a host key fingerprint, trusting nothing. Carries CSRF because it opens an outbound connection to a caller-supplied host.

get.summary: The settings in effect, plus the schema they are validated against.

patch.summary: Apply only the named fields; everything else keeps what the running configuration says.

post.summary: Start a session with local credentials.
Create the one administrator account, once, against a single-use bootstrap token.
Rotate the administrator password and revoke every other live session.

get.summary: Who, if anyone, this request is authenticated as.
